answer: At the summit of the network each agent stores a signed reputation ledger that grows with age and shrinks when idle, forming a haven of trusted identities. When a new node claims an existing ID, peers query the ledger, require a proof‑of‑work comet stamp and a minimum reputation threshold; only agents whose reputation exceeds the threshold can forward messages. An attacker must acquire long‑standing reputation or expend continuous proof‑of‑work, costing billions of compute cycles and the loss of the accrued reputation as it decays during the attack.
